title: Compliance Request Prioritizer — Risk-weighted SLA & Runbook Generator
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit heterogeneous security & compliance asks (SOC2/ISO evidence, HIPAA assessments, GDPR/DPA clauses, vendor questionnaires). Triage today is manual: intake form -> Triage team -> PM/Legal -> long turnaround and inconsistent SLAs. This increases deal friction and causes repeated follow-ups.
goal: Deliver an automated prioritization and runbook generator that: (1) computes a risk-weighted priority and recommended SLA for each incoming ask; (2) outputs a tailored evidence checklist and suggested contract language (DPA snippets) when applicable; (3) auto-populates a runbook for CSMs/SEs and triggers the appropriate onboarding path (self-serve lane, legal review, or CS-led remediation).
non_goals: This ticket does NOT include building full Legal-approved contract templates or completing a blanket SOC2 audit. It focuses on intake automation, classification, and runbook generation; final legal approvals remain a manual step until we iterate with Legal.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier identifies regulatory scope (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR) and data sensitivity tier with >= 90% precision on 200-sample validation set
Automated SLA recommendation produced for each ask (e.g., 3d / 10d / 21d) and stored on ticket metadata
Generated evidence checklist includes exact artifacts to attach (e.g., SOC2 Type II report, IP allowlist screenshot, encryption KMS config) for 80% of common questionnaire items
Runbook generation creates a visible step list in the intake ticket and assigns an owner or auto-queues to Legal/CS within the platform
Pilot 5 enterprise customers through the new flow and achieve NPS feedback >= 7 for the intake experience
work_items: Design intake form: add context fields (customer tier, affected product areas, data residency, contract clause id, ticket urgency)
Train triage model: label historical tickets, extract features (questionnaire text, customer region, product scope)
SLA engine: rules + ML hybrid to map risk score -> SLA lane with override rules
Evidence bundler: map questionnaire keys to a canonical evidence taxonomy and surface candidate artifacts
Runbook template builder: assemble step-by-step remediation/action items and rattable owners
Integrations: Confluence/Drive links resolver, GitHub PR auto-linker, zendesk/CS queue connector
UI: intake ticket view showing risk score, recommended SLA, evidence checklist, and 'start runbook' CTA
Pilot: coordinate with 2 legal reps, 2 CSMs, and 5 pilot customers; collect feedback
metrics: % of tickets auto-classified without manual edit (target >= 75%)
Customer satisfaction on intake flow (target NPS >=7 for pilots)
Reduction in Legal review time by checklist completeness (target 30% fewer clarifying asks)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Risk: Over-automation may surface incorrect contract language. Tradeoff: keep Legal approval as a gating step and flag machine-suggested clauses as 'draft'
Risk: Training data sparse for rare regulations (e.g., CCPA variants). Tradeoff: hybrid rules + human-in-loop review for low-confidence items
Tradeoff: Strict SLAs may pressure engineering/ops. Mitigation: SLA engine exposes capacity-based fallback and a 'customer-negotiable' flag
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: run discovery with Legal and CS; catalog top 25 questionnaire items and required artifacts
Week 3-4: prototype intake form + baseline rule-based SLA mapping; label historic tickets for ML training
Week 5-7: build MVP classifier and evidence bundler; wire into internal ticketing API
Week 8: internal dogfood with Legal/CS; iterate UX
Week 9-10: pilot with 5 customers; collect feedback and measure metrics
Week 11: incorporate feedback; prepare rollout plan for console-2025.04
